extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and meta-researchers studying peer review; dataset users and developers of NLP models for review analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Construction, annotation, analysis and NLP-task framing of a dataset of scientific peer reviews (PeerRead) covering top-tier NLP/ML/AI venues and arXiv; includes reviewer-instruction-derived aspect rubrics, dataset inclusion rules, preprocessing, and model features for acceptance and aspect-score prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper fit in ACL 2016? (Answer in light of desire to broaden the scope of research areas represented at ACL.) 5: Certainly. 4: Probably. 3: Unsure. 2: Probably not. 1: Certainly not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided as part of reviewer instructions (Appendix B). In annotation, when review comments do not address a specific aspect, 'not discussed' is used. Note authors caution that in annotation process, reviewers probably only address appropriateness explicitly when the paper is inappropriate, introducing negative bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the reasonably well-prepared reader, is it clear what was done and why? Is the paper well-written and well-structured? 5 = Very clear. 4 = Understandable by most readers. 3 = Mostly understandable with some effort. 2 = Important questions were hard to resolve even with effort. 1 = Much of the paper is confusing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as one of the aspect scores; correlates with overall recommendation (ρ=0.42 in ACL 2017). Review length sometimes considered a proxy for review quality; annotators only considered review text when inferring aspect scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: How original is the approach? Does this paper break new ground in topic, methodology, or content? How exciting and innovative is the research it describes? Scale from 1 (work done before / done better) to 5 (surprising; significant new problem/technique/insight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper could score high on originality even if results don't show convincing benefit. In analysis, 'originality' had high variance and was one of the aspects where models improved over mean baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical Soundness / Correctness (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the technical approach sound and well-chosen? Can one trust the empirical claims—are they supported by proper experiments and correctly interpreted? 5 = claims convincingly supported; 1 = fatally flawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of reviewer instruction aspects. Used in correlation analysis (soundness/correctness had low correlation with final recommendation, ρ≈0.01 in ACL 2017).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical Soundness / Correctness (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the mathematical approach sound and well-chosen? Are the arguments cogent and well-supported? 5 = very apt and convincing; 1 = fatally flawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate aspect for theoretical work in reviewer instructions; treated analogously to empirical soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful Comparison (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the authors make clear where the problems and methods sit with respect to existing literature? Are references adequate? For empirical papers, are results meaningfully compared with best prior approaches? 5 = precise and complete comparison; 1 = little awareness or lacks necessary empirical comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in annotated aspects; in ACL 2017/ICLR analyses it appears with varied coverage (e.g., ~49% of reviews discussed 'originality' while only 5% discussed 'appropriateness').

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this paper have enough substance, or would it benefit from more ideas or results? This mainly concerns the amount of work (distinct from quality). 5 = more ideas/results than most publications; 1 = seems thin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ACL 2017, 'substance' correlated most strongly with the overall recommendation (ρ=0.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Ideas or Results (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: How significant is the work described? If ideas are novel, will they be useful or inspirational? Will the paper bring new insights? 5 = will affect the field; 1 = no impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an aspect score. Also split into related sub-aspects in reviewer instructions for accompanying software and datasets (see separate metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Accompanying Software (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If software was submitted or released with the paper, what is the expected impact of the software package? 5 = enabling; 1 = no usable software released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance defines usefulness spectrum (enabling/useful/potentially useful/documentary/no usable software).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Accompanying Dataset (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dataset was submitted or released with the paper, what is the expected impact of the dataset? 5 = enabling; 1 = no usable datasets submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same graded guidance as for software. Annotators used these definitions when assigning aspect scores based on review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation / Overall Recommendation (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric value characterizing whether the draft should be accepted for the venue (5 = strong accept / changed thinking; 1 = poor / fight to have it rejected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are asked to integrate their aspect scores into this final value. Analysis shows overall recommendation correlates most with 'substance' and 'clarity' and least with 'soundness' and 'originality'. Recommendation also correlates with presentation-format suggestions (oral recommendations have higher overall recommendation scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Confidence (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: How confident is the reviewer in their evaluation (5 = positive evaluation is correct; 1 = not my area / educated guess).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captured in reviewer metadata; available in some sources (e.g., NIPS confidence 1–3, OpenReview confidence 1–5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect-score Annotation Guidelines (annotation protocol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotate seven aspects (appropriateness, clarity, originality, soundness/correctness, meaningful comparison, substance, impact) by reading only the review text and selecting an integer score 1–5; use a special 'not discussed' value when the review doesn't address the aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators were provided instructions given to ACL 2016 reviewers for each aspect. Feasibility study showed annotators could infer about half of aspect scores from text; mean absolute difference vs. gold was 0.51 on 1–5 scale when aspect was discussed. Re-annotation consistency: 77% consistent (same or ±1), 2% off by ≥2, 21% cases where one annotation was 'not discussed' and the other not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opted-in review inclusion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission is included in the opted-in sections only if (i) the corresponding author opts-in the paper draft, and (ii) at least one of the reviewers opts-in their anonymous reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied for CoNLL 2016 and ACL 2017; resulted in only papers/reviews where both conditions held (e.g., 39 reviews for 22 CoNLL submissions; 275 reviews for 137 ACL submissions). Opt-in process may bias included reviews toward higher quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review metadata dimensions and scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may include textual comments, numerical recommendation scores and confidence levels. Examples: NIPS reviews include textual comments and confidence (1–3); OpenReview includes numerical recommendations (1–10) and confidence (1–5); opted-in ACL/CoNLL reviews include aspect scores (1–5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different sources provide different metadata; when annotating, the authors used only official assigned reviews and excluded unofficial comments, author responses, and meta-reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: arXiv acceptance / probably-rejected labeling criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to assign 'accepted' and 'probably-rejected' labels to arXiv submissions relative to a set of target venues (ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, EACL, TACL, NIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted: match arXiv to DBLP entries by title/author Jaccard distance (Sutton & Gong 2017) and add matches with relative Levenshtein distance < 0.1. Probably-rejected requires: paper not accepted to any target venue; arXiv category in cs.cl, cs.lg or cs.ai; not cross-listed in non-cs categories; submission date within one month of target venue deadlines; submission date coincides with at least one arXiv paper accepted for a target venue. Sanity checks found low false-negative rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset organization & preprocessing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerRead v1.0 organized into sections (CoNLL 2016, ACL 2017, ICLR 2017, NIPS 2013–2017, arXiv 2007–2017). Papers split into training/dev/test with 0.9:0.05:0.05 ratios. For each paper include PDF and extracted textual content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text extraction used the Science Parse library. Each split is represented as a JSON list of paper objects containing paper details, accept/reject/probably-reject label, and list of reviews. Different sections may have different license agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation format (oral vs poster) decision guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Program chairs recommend deciding oral vs. poster based on expected size of interested audience and whether the ideas can be grasped without back-and-forth discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis of ACL 2017 reviews shows reviewers recommending oral presentations give on average 0.9 higher overall recommendation scores and higher substance/clarity, suggesting reviewers favor stronger, more accessible papers for oral slots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review length as a proxy for review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Review length (words) is reported and is often thought of as a measure of review quality; ACL 2017 average review length ~531 words vs ICLR 2017 ~346 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note that opt-in selection (ACL reviews opted-in) likely biases ACL reviews toward longer/higher-quality reviews; so length is only a noisy proxy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation diagnostics between overall recommendation and aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Pairwise Pearson correlation between overall recommendation and aspect scores (ACL 2017): Substance 0.59, Clarity 0.42, Appropriateness 0.30, Impact 0.16, Meaningful comparison 0.15, Originality 0.08, Soundness/Correctness 0.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to highlight which aspects most strongly influence final recommendations; informs what aspects models should prioritize when predicting recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coarse & lexical features for acceptance classification (feature set)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of 22 coarse features and lexical representations used to predict paper acceptance: abstract_contains_X (keywords like deep, neural, state_of_the_art, novel, outperform), title_length, num_authors, most_recent_refs_year, num_refs, num_refmentions, avg_length_refs_mention, num_recent_refs, num_ref_to_X (counts of figures/tables/sections/equations/theorems), num_uniq_words, num_sections, avg_sentence_length, contains_appendix, prop_of_freq_words, BOW, BOW+TFIDF, GloVe average, GloVe+TFIDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ablation showed highly salient features: presence of appendix, number of theorems/equations, avg length of context before a citation (avg_len_ref), number of recent references (#recent_refs), presence of abstract phrases (e.g., 'state_of_the_art' or 'neural'), and title length. Models used hand-engineered features (22 coarse features) plus lexical/dense features and standard ML classifiers (logistic regression, SVM, Random Forest, etc.).
